original_question: If (X, d) is completely metrizable, with no separability assumption, is that equivalent to some completeness-type topological property of the Wijsman hyperspace (2^X, T_W(d))?
target_in_paper: Section 3, Problem 3.1: the paper’s second main open problem on completeness-type properties of Wijsman hyperspaces.
correct_elements: Your draft is very close to the paper’s actual target. It correctly identifies the relevant objects—complete metrizability, the absence of a separability assumption, and the Wijsman hyperspace (2^X, T_W(d))—and it asks exactly the kind of equivalence posed in the paper’s Section 3.
missing_details: The paper’s official target is an open problem, namely Problem 3.1 in Section 3, not a theorem or conjecture.
The notation 2^X needs to be made explicit: in this paper it denotes the family of all nonempty closed subsets of X.
The Wijsman topology T_W(d) should be defined stand-alone: it is the topology on 2^X induced by the distance maps A -> d(x,A) for x in X.
The official wording is about complete metrizability without separability; your draft has the right idea, but the stand-alone version should say this explicitly rather than leaving it parenthetical.

To match the paper faithfully, the question should not presuppose a specific named completeness property; the point is whether there is some completeness-type property of the Wijsman hyperspace that characterizes complete metrizability.

Your draft does not distinguish the broad Problem 3.1 from later, more specific follow-up questions in the same section about being strongly Choquet or strongly alpha-favorable; the refined question should stay with the broader Problem 3.1 unless one explicitly chooses those later specializations.

Nearby context in Section 3 shows that Cech-completeness and, more generally, closed-hereditary completeness-type properties are already ruled out as candidates; that context matters for understanding why the problem is phrased so broadly.
refined_question: Let (X,d) be a metric space, and let 2^X denote the set of all nonempty closed subsets of X, endowed with the Wijsman topology T_{W(d)} induced by the distance functionals A -> d(x,A) for x in X. Without assuming separability, is the complete metrizability of X equivalent to the possession by the Wijsman hyperspace (2^X, T_{W(d)}) of some completeness-type topological property?
justification: The draft matches Problem 3.1 almost verbatim. Section 1 introduces the notation 2^X and T_{W(d)} and explicitly says that the paper’s second main problem is whether the Wijsman topology induced by a completely metrizable metric has some completeness-type properties. Section 3 then states the exact open problem as Problem 3.1. The surrounding discussion explains why the question must remain broad: Costantini’s example rules out Cech-completeness, and Theorem 3.2 shows that no closed-hereditary completeness-type property can solve the problem. Theorem 3.5 provides only a partial answer in the restricted class of locally separable metrizable spaces, so the refined question should remain the general Problem 3.1 rather than being narrowed to strong Choquet or strong alpha-favorability.
